'''Taurean Waller-Prince''' (born March 22, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor Bears]]. 

== High school career ==
Prince played three seasons of high school basketball under head coach Jim Weaver at [[Earl Warren High School]] in [[San Antonio, Texas]]. As a senior, he led the team to the state semifinals. He originally chose to play [[college basketball]] with the [[LIU-Brooklyn Blackbirds men's basketball|LIU-Brooklyn Blackbirds]], but switched to [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] due to a coaching change within the former program.<ref name=bio />

== Collegiate career ==
Prince played 24 games off the bench in his freshman season. He finished the year averaging 3.7 points and 2.2 rebounds in 6.4 minutes per game. In the spring prior to his sophomore season, Prince was on the [[Big 12 Conference]] Commissioner's Honor Roll. After averaging 6.2 points and 2.8 rebounds in 14.2 minutes per game and appearing in all 38 of [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]]'s games, he won the Big 12 Sixth Man Award and earned all-conference honors.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Taurean Prince bio|url=http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/taurean_prince_821205.html|website=''BaylorBears.com''|accessdate=6 August 2015}}</ref> Entering his third season, [[Fran Fraschilla]] labeled him as a strong candidate for [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] in [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16]].<ref name=panam>{{cite web|last1=Hodge|first1=Ashley|title=Taurean Waller-Prince helps lead USA to bronze medal at PanAm|url=http://baylor.247sports.com/Bolt/Taurean-Waller-Prince-helps-lead-USA-to-bronze-medal-at-PanAm-38385209|website=[[247Sports.com]]|accessdate=6 August 2015}}</ref>His 2016 season ended against Yale when he tried to 'spider dunk' and was called for a technical foul.

== International career ==
In the summer of 2015, following his sophomore season, Prince helped the [[United States men's national basketball team]] win the bronze medal at the [[2015 Pan American Games]]. He was on a team led by [[Bobby Brown (basketball)|Bobby Brown]] and [[Anthony Randolph]].<ref name=panam />
